item.title: Out-of-time-order hydrodynamics and scrambling
item.description: arXiv:2610.16888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hydrodynamics as an effective field theory (EFT) has been immensely successful for predicting the behaviour of time-ordered correlation functions in the long-time, large-distance regime. In this paper, we analyse the predictions of hydrodynamics for scrambling as probed by out-of-time order correlators (OTOCs). To do so, we consider an all-derivative order generalisation of the Schwinger-Keldysh EFT of hydrodynamics extended to a four-fold time contour required to capture OTOCs. A crucial ingredient of the construction is a local SL(2,R) symmetry, which has previously been suggested as a mechanism for scrambling. We also derive this exact EFT from the microscopic formulation of the maximally chaotic low-temperature limit of the SYK lattice, thereby determining all transport coefficients for this model. As a novel application, we compute the OTOC of energy currents, find that its exponential growth saturates the chaos bound, and match it to expectations based on a shockwave (or scramblon) effective description. Our work shows that the universality of hydrodynamics degrees of freedom extends beyond traditional time-ordered correlators to more complex observables such as OTOCs.
item.dc:creator: Marta Bucca, Akash Jain, M\'ark Mezei, Alexey Milekhin

item.title: Microscopic Modeling of Interlayer Tunneling in Twisted Bilayer Cuprates
item.description: arXiv:2610.16930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The field of twistronics, recently extended to twisted bilayer cuprate systems, has generated considerable interest due to the prediction of $d+id'$ states close to a $45^\circ$ twist, as suggested by multiple experimental probes. Theoretical studies of these systems using a variety of models and many-body theoretical techniques have revealed multiple competing order parameters. The large variability in experimental results and theoretical predictions demands an accurate microscopic model for these systems, in particular a more realistic description of the interlayer tunneling. In this study, we fit the in-plane hopping and compute the interlayer tunneling amplitudes by calculating the orbital overlap between $d_{x^2-y^2}$ wave functions at each site of the twisted square-lattice model. We observe sign-changing tunneling amplitudes, a strong twist-angle dependence of the direct tunneling term, and long-range tunneling amplitudes that often dominate over direct tunneling. We investigate the band structure, Fermi surfaces, and spectral functions in comparison with those obtained from the phenomenological model and find a substantial redistribution of spectral weight that modifies the competition between different superconducting ground states. We determine the phase diagram as a function of twist angle, filling, and direct tunneling strength, which is controlled by the $c$-axis distance between the monolayers, and observe a reduction in the region of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking (TRSB) $d+id'$ states compared with the phenomenological model. Finally, we investigate the Josephson critical current across the phase diagram and find strongly suppressed critical currents close to a $45^\circ$ twist, consistent with experimental observations.
item.dc:creator: Siddhant Panda, Andreas Kreisel, Laura Fanfarillo, P. J. Hirschfeld

item.title: Entanglement Sudden Death in Gapped Ground States
item.description: arXiv:2610.17038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial sudden death of entanglement refers to the disappearance of quantum correlations between subsystems after a certain distance called the entanglement length. Specifically, given a density matrix $\rho_{ABC}$ on a tripartite system $ABC$ with $B$ spatially separating $A$ and $C$, the entanglement length is the distance $\ell(A,C)$ after which the reduced density matrix $\rho_{AC}$, given by tracing out the $B$ subsystem, is separable. We show in the case of gapped ground states in any dimension that the entanglement length is finite on finite subsystems. Restricting to one-dimensional systems, we prove that normal matrix product states have a finite entanglement length independent of $A$ and $C$, and that a finite pure state with such uniform entanglement length has a matrix product state representation with bond dimension independent of $A$ and $C$. Consequently, in one dimension, entanglement length distinguishes matrix product states from all other pure states.
item.dc:creator: Robert Ferydouni, Thomas Jackson, Samuel O. Scalet

item.title: Fermionic non-Gaussianity via computable measures and experimentally accessible bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.17219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interacting fermions owe both their non-trivial correlations and their computational power to their departure from Gaussianity. Yet, quantifying that departure geometrically faces two challenges: the Gaussian manifold is non-convex, and perturbative treatments are confined to weak interactions. Here, we introduce a geometric measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity, the fidelity distance of a target state to the manifold of fermionic Gaussian states. We construct an iteration formalism to numerically access it, applicable also at strong coupling. Further, we prove a sharpened operator Jensen inequality, of interest in its own right. We use it to derive a witness that involves only two- and four-point fermionic correlators. Numerical benchmarks on the one-dimensional Fermi--Hubbard model show that the quality of the witness improves with system size and, for strong coupling, is tighter than antiflatness. Our results open a scalable route to charting non-Gaussianity of strongly-interacting fermionic quantum simulators.
item.dc:creator: Leela Ganesh Chandra Lakkaraju, Naga Dileep Varikuti, Philipp Hauke

item.title: Krylov Complexity and Quantum Many-body Scars in Non-Hermitian Kinetically Constrained Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.17328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermalization in closed quantum systems and its breakdown are central to understanding the emergence of statistical behavior in isolated many-body systems. Kinetic constraints can hinder thermalization by restricting the allowed dynamics and giving rise to non-ergodic behavior. While various aspects of ergodicity breaking in kinetically constrained models have been extensively studied in Hermitian systems, their behavior in non-Hermitian kinetically constrained models remains less explored. In particular, the inequivalence of left and right eigenstate ensembles in non-Hermitian systems raises the question of whether they exhibit qualitatively different dynamical and eigenstate properties. In this work, we study non-Hermitian generalizations of the paradigmatic PXP and PPXPP models, focusing on their Krylov complexity, eigenstate structure, and dynamics. By exploiting the Arnoldi's algorithm, we find distinct behavior of Krylov complexity in the left and right eigenstate ensembles as non-Hermiticity is increased: in the right ensemble, it exhibits persistent oscillations with an increasing period, while in the left ensemble, it gradually saturates. The characteristic arch-shaped profile of the Arnoldi coefficients is also modified differently in the two ensembles, with a Hermitian-like arch re-emerging in the left ensemble at large non Hermiticity. Additionally, in the non-Hermitian PXP model, the right ensemble retains the characteristic scar structure, while the left ensemble develops additional non-scar eigenstates with anomalously low entanglement and large overlap with the vacuum state. These findings reveal that non-Hermiticity can affect Krylov dynamics and eigenstate structure differently in the left and right ensembles, demonstrating the need to treat them separately when characterizing non-Hermitian kinetically constrained systems.
item.dc:creator: Arkaprava Sil, Rudraksh Kaushik, Souvik Kundu, Prasant Mallik, Sudipto Singha Roy

item.title: Crystal growth, magnetic, and transport properties of the candidate altermagnet Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Altermagnetism is a rapidly emerging paradigm in condensed matter magnetism, yet the number of experimentally confirmed altermagnetic candidates remains remarkably limited. Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$ has long been theoretically proposed as a promising altermagnet, but there are no reports on experimental investigation of single crystals. Here, we report the successful growth of high-quality single crystals of Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$ and present its structural, thermal, magnetic, and transport properties. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction provides detailed crystallographic information and confirms the hexagonal crystal symmetry ($P6_3/mmc$), one of the criteria for altermagnetic behavior. Resistivity and heat capacity measurements unambiguously identify an antiferromagnetic N\'{e}el temperature of $T_N \sim 141$ K. Magnetotransport measurements reveal non-trivial features in the magnetoresistance and Hall response, indicative of quantum diffusive transport phenomena. Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$, synthesized here for the first time in single-crystalline form, therefore serves as an experimental platform for probing the rich spectrum of phenomena predicted for altermagnetic materials.
item.dc:creator: Nashra Pistawala, Martin R. Lees, Geetha Balakrishnan, Daniel A. Mayoh

item.title: Observation of stacked vortex structure with number controllable Majorana zero mode in Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$/FeTe heterojunction
item.description: arXiv:2610.17701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Creation and control of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) in solid devices is the key challenge in realizing fault tolerant topological quantum computation. Here we report spectroscopic evidence for number controllable MZMs in stoichiometric one quintuple layer Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$/FeTe heterostructures, together with the observation of stacked vortices in superconducting islands. Low temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy reveal a long period moire superlattice arising from lattice mismatch, which induces nanoscale modulation of superconducting gaps. Magnetic vortices exhibit a stacked core structure with two layer derived bound state branches: a dispersive branch evolving into an X-shaped pattern away from the vortex center, and a quantum-limit branch characterized by a spatially unsplit MZMs together with discrete integer quantized Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states. Notably, MZMs are observed in all measured vortices, and their number can be tuned by magnetic field and the size of Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$ islands. These results establish stoichiometric 1QL-Bi$_{2}$Te$_{3}$/FeTe as a patterned superconducting interface that enables isolated and few-vortex Majorana configurations, providing a controlled platform for fuse MZMs.
item.dc:creator: Xinru Han, Zhaokun Luo, Quanxin Hu, Xingjian Zhu, Xiaohong Pan, Dan Mu, Xinyu Liang, Zulin Xu, Qiheng Wang, Ryan L. Kong, Mingyuan Li, Zhengliang Zhang, Fazhi Yang, Mojun Pan, Xin Liu, Qiangqiang Gu, Baiqing Lv, Gan Wang, Hong Ding

item.title: Local error correction prolongs time-crystalline memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.18124v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discrete time crystals are non-equilibrium phases of matter with spatiotemporal order and a response that breaks the time-translation symmetry of a periodic external drive. Interactions, spatial disorder and correlated random driving can in theory stabilize this order. In experiments, however, coupling to the environment limits the time crystal lifetime. Here we use stochastic local bit-flip error correction to prolong the time-crystalline response of a driven, spatially disordered two-dimensional Ising model on a superconducting quantum processor, using a repetition code with distances three and five on a honeycomb lattice with up to 68 physical qubits. Even though ancilla qubits, midcircuit syndrome measurements and decoding increase the required quantum and classical resources, the stochastic drive increases the memory decay time by a factor of up to two. At late times we observe that recovery stabilizes spatial order across the lattice. The spin-configuration distributions explain this separation, as recovery suppresses disagreeing bonds while broadening occupies completely reversed states. Syndrome measurements without correction accelerate the memory decay, demonstrating the importance of conditional correction. Our results show that local bit-flip error correction can preserve time-crystalline memory over more drive cycles than the bare dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Benedikt Fauseweh

item.title: Coherent Phonon Generation from Prethermal Carrier Populations in a Semiconductor
item.description: arXiv:2610.18279v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. Fitting this model to the data yields an excited transition state lifetime of a few femtoseconds. These results identify transition selectivity, rather than a thermalized total carrier density, as a key factor controlling coherent-phonon generation in semiconductors excited near a band gap.
item.dc:creator: Mingyu Shi, Matteo Savoini, Patrick Friebel, Andrea Annunziata, Thomas Metzger, Yunpei Deng, Laura Cattaneo, Steven L. Johnson

item.title: Explicitly correlated ground states with a feedback-free variational hybrid algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2610.18681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Explicitly correlated methods, which represent dominant short-range correlations by a diagonal Jastrow-type correlator, are designed to accurately describe systems of strongly correlated electrons, such as the fully periodic 2D Fermi--Hubbard model. However, as the reference state is compact in momentum space whereas the correlator acts naturally in real space, there is a fundamental mismatch of bases that classical algorithms resolve only by restricting the reference or the correlator. Here we propose a hybrid algorithm in which a quantum processor prepares a low-entanglement momentum-space matrix product state (MPS), precomputed classically by the transcorrelated method at the cost of a nonvariational energy, rotates it to real space, and measures in bases fixed by the Hamiltonian. Because the measurement bases are independent of the correlator, the correlator can be variationally optimized entirely in classical post-processing with no quantum-classical feedback loop. We demonstrate our algorithm on 32 qubits of Quantinuum's H2-2 with a bond-dimension-4 MPS for the half-filled $4 \times 4$ lattice and achieve a relative ground-state energy error of $16 \pm 4\%$ after postselection, reduced to $3.5 \pm 0.5\%$ by calibration using low-order moments from the MPS. Compared with other feedback-free hybrid algorithms, even under generous assumptions, our method requires fewer samples than quantum-selected configuration interaction and fewer two-qubit gates than quantum Krylov methods.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Corbett, Akimasa Miyake

item.title: Emergent Loop Geometry in Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.18742v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gauge-equivariant graph neural networks generate ordered products of gauge links through local message passing, but the geometry of these internal structures is not captured by the receptive field alone. We investigate the statistical ensemble of closed lattice walks generated by recursive node- and edge-feature operations, independently of network training. Analytical and numerical results reveal a separation between rapid growth of contour length and much slower spatial expansion: deeper compositions generate increasingly long paths through repeated traversal of relatively compact regions. Loop expansions of fermionic observables provide a physical interpretation of this hierarchy, showing how spatial locality remains compatible with high-order dependence on nearby gauge fields. These findings identify complementary roles of network depth in extending spatial reach and enriching the representations constructed within that reach, providing a geometrical perspective on learning lattice gauge observables.
item.dc:creator: Ali Rayat, Gia-Wei Chern

item.title: Fermion-fermion interaction driven phase transitions in rhombohedral trilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2406.01877v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The effects of short-range fermion-fermion interactions on the low-energy properties of rhombohedral trilayer graphene are comprehensively investigated using the momentum-shell renormalization group method. We take into account all one-loop corrections and establish the energy-dependent coupled evolutions of independent fermionic couplings that carry the physical information stemming from the interplay of various fermion-fermion interactions. With detailed numerical analysis, we observe that the ferocious competition among all fermion-fermion interactions can drive fermionic couplings to four distinct fixed points, dubbed $\textrm{FP}_{1}$, $\textrm{FP}_{2}$, $\textrm{FP}_{3}$, and $\textrm{FP}_{4}$, in the interaction-parameter space. These fixed points primarily dictate the fate of the system in the low-energy regime and are always associated with some instabilities characterized by specific symmetry breakings, leading to certain phase transitions. To determine the favorable states arising from the potential phase transitions, we introduce a number of fermion-bilinear source terms to characterize the underlying candidate states. By comparing their related susceptibilities, we find that the dominant states correspond to spin-singlet superconductivity, spin-triplet pair-density-waves, and spin-triplet superconductivity for fixed points $\textrm{FP}_{1,3}$, $\textrm{FP}_{2}$, and $\textrm{FP}_{4}$, respectively. These provide valuable insights into the low-energy properties of rhombohedral trilayer graphene and analogous materials.
item.dc:creator: Qiao-Chu Zhang, Jing Wang

item.title: CoS++: Towards More General and Explicit Implementations for Sampling High-Order Feynman Diagrammatic Series
item.description: arXiv:2507.12349v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend combinatorial summation (CoS) of connected Feynman diagrams to Hubbard mod- els with flavor-dependent propagators and counterterm shifts. The construction combines an interaction-occupancy mask with labels for the open fermion cycle, allowing equivalent endpoint his- tories to be accumulated while retaining the flavor and sublattice information needed by subsequent contractions. In the flavor-dependent version, denoted symmetry-broken CoS (SB-CoS), normal heads carry the cycle flavor and counterterm heads inherit the flavor at their interaction partner. We prove the correctness of the resulting recurrence and introduce terminal readouts that return all nonempty interaction-subset values from a shared circuit, as required by a many-configuration Markov-chain sampler. For three flavors, a second formulation uses determinant polynomials and a local interaction tensor, with connected coefficients extracted by subset recursion or Fourier interpo- lation and a support sieve. Applications to the two-spin honeycomb and three-flavor square-lattice Hubbard models illustrate the treatment of sublattice structure and non-uniform reference shifts.
item.dc:creator: Boyuan Shi

item.title: Anyon polarons as a window into the competing phases of the Kitaev-Gamma-Gamma-prime model
item.description: arXiv:2508.21129v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the dispersions of anyon quasiparticles in the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid perturbed by $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ couplings in order to understand phase transitions into competing states through anyon gap-closing instabilities. We demonstrate how anyon gap closings provide a way to understand phase transitions into a plethora of previously identified competing phases---including zigzag, stripy, $120^\circ$, and incommensurate spiral phases---and are in agreement with numerical studies not only on the nature of the phases, but also on the specific critical values of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ couplings. Remarkably, when the antiferromagnetic Kitaev model is perturbed by a negative $\Gamma$ interaction, we find that the single-vison and fermion gaps remain open while the gap of a magnon-like local boson vanishes. This points to a plausible candidate coexistence regime where long-range magnetic order emerges while fractionalized excitations inherited from the Kitaev spin liquid may persist. The magnetic order can be either stripy antiferromagnetic or incommensurate spiral, depending on the sign of $\Gamma'$.
item.dc:creator: Chuan Chen, Inti Sodemann Villadiego

item.title: Limitations of Avila-inspired theory in the diamond chain with quasiperiodic disorder
item.description: arXiv:2603.12362v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The mobility edges (MEs) that separate localized, multifractal and ergodic states in energy are a central concept in understanding Anderson localization. In this work we study the effect of several mutually commensurate quasiperiodic frequencies on the mobility edge formation. We focus on the example of the addition of a constant offset to the quasiperiodic potential of the one-dimensional all-bands-flat diamond chain. We show that this additional offset can transform the anomalous mobility edges (AMEs), i.e. the energies, separating localized and multifractal states, into conventional mobility edges, separating localized from delocalized states. Also this appears to be the first example which shows the inability of Avila's global theory to analytically predict the ME location. We observe this both quantitatively, through the ME location mismatch, and qualitatively, via the formation of multiple MEs, not predicted by the theory.
item.dc:creator: Manish Kumar, Ivan M. Khaymovich, Auditya Sharma

item.title: Crystal-Field Symmetry Constraints in Layered Honeycomb ErBr$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2604.24951v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Crystal-field symmetry restricts the ground-state Kramers doublet of ErBr$_3$ to one of two classes. We show that the compressed octahedral environment selects the class with $\langle \psi_\pm | J^{\pm} | \psi_\mp \rangle = 0$, suppressing the lowest-order $J^{\pm}$-mediated exchange. Thermodynamic measurements reveal two zero-field anomalies at 0.375 and 0.200 K. Under an in-plane magnetic field, the thermodynamic response separates into a phase boundary and a broader crossover line. Inelastic neutron scattering measurements at 2 K reveal no well-defined low-energy dispersive magnetic modes. These results connect the ground-state symmetry with the field-dependent thermodynamic response of ErBr$_3$, providing a microscopic starting point for understanding its low-energy magnetic behavior.
item.dc:creator: Biaoyan Hu, Mingyuan Hu, Franz Demmel, Andrey A. Podlesnyak, Jiaqing He, Liusuo Wu

item.title: Boundary-dependent topological degeneracy in an Ising chain
item.description: arXiv:2605.09510v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The influence of boundary conditions on bulk properties is generally expected to vanish in the thermodynamic limit. Here we show that this expectation can fail in an open transverse field Ising chain with modified boundary fields. By removing only the transverse fields acting on the two edge spins while leaving the bulk Hamiltonian unchanged, we uncover a boundary-induced switching of the topological spectral degeneracy. In contrast to the conventional open chain, where the topological degeneracy occurs in the ferromagnetic phase ($\left\vert g\right\vert <1$), the modified boundary condition shifts it to the paramagnetic phase ($\left\vert g\right\vert >1$). We demonstrate that the underlying mechanism originates from two exact local conserved quantities associated with the edge spins, which partition the Hilbert space into invariant sectors. Based on this structure, we establish an exact description in terms of domain-wall excitations, under which the Hamiltonian decomposes into two independent Kitaev chains. Complementarily, the Majorana representation reveals that the spectral switching originates from different unit-cell conventions and boundary terminations of the corresponding effective SSH lattice, leading to distinct boundary zero-mode structures without altering the bulk Hamiltonian. Furthermore, we show that the boundary-induced topological degeneracy remains observable at finite temperatures through non-Hermitian quench dynamics, providing a dynamical manifestation of the bulk-boundary correspondence. These results demonstrate that boundary engineering, through the introduction of local conserved boundary degrees of freedom, provides an effective route for controlling topological degeneracy in quantum spin chains without modifying bulk interactions.
item.dc:creator: E. S. Ma, Z. Song

item.title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints for hyperbolic lattices
item.description: arXiv:2605.15974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem and its higher-dimensional extensions forbid the existence of a unique, symmetric, and gapped ground state at fractional fillings in quantum many-body systems with a conserved particle number (or spin angular momentum) and the conventional translation symmetry of Euclidean lattices. In this work, we propose a generalization of the LSM theorem to quantum many-body systems on hyperbolic lattices, i.e., regular tessellations of two-dimensional negatively curved space. By leveraging concepts from hyperbolic band theory in a many-body setting, we adapt Oshikawa's flux-threading argument to periodic hyperbolic lattices with a non-Euclidean (Fuchsian) translation symmetry and compute a lower-bound to the ground-state degeneracy as a function of filling and lattice geometry. We explore the consequences of LSM constraints for gapped phases of hyperbolic quantum matter and suggest frustrated spin models on hyperbolic analogs of the square and triangular lattices as promising platforms for realizing symmetric spin liquids in hyperbolic space.
item.dc:creator: G. Shankar, Joseph Maciejko

item.title: Diagrammatic Monte Carlo for Fermionic R\'enyi Entanglement Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2605.21632v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a direct diagrammatic Monte Carlo method for the second R\'enyi entropy of inter- acting lattice fermions. Fermionic replica sewing yields a connected-determinant (CDet) expansion, which we sample with many-configuration Markov-chain Monte Carlo. On a 3 \times 3 Hubbard clus- ter, deterministic coefficients through third order agree with exact-diagonalization derivatives for three reference shifts, while sampling extends the series to tenth order. For a reference shift with a continuous stability region, conformal-Borel resummation also gives good agreement with the exact entropy. We further compute coefficients through ninth order on 40 \times 40 and 50 \times 50 periodic lat- tices, with subsystems of up to 676 sites. The resummed results from different reference shifts show good agreement at a common truncation order. Their shift and order dependence provide checks on the stability of the continuation. These calculations extend connected-diagram sampling to spatial R\'enyi observables on large finite fermionic systems.
item.dc:creator: Boyuan Shi

item.title: Thermal Signatures of the Slater-Mott Crossover in the Hubbard Model: From Double Occupancy to Antiferromagnetic Correlation Length
item.description: arXiv:2606.10976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The interaction-driven crossover from a Slater insulator to a Mott insulator in the N\'{e}el-ordered ground state of the Hubbard model is a fundamental paradigm of strongly correlated electrons, yet its quantitative characterization has remained elusive. Here we establish a clear and experimentally accessible thermal criterion for this crossover via the sign change of the temperature derivative of double occupancy, $(\partial D/\partial T)_U$, near zero temperature. In the Slater regime, $(\partial D/\partial T)_U>0$ reflects the major role of charge fluctuations; in the Mott regime, the anomalous $(\partial D/\partial T)_U<0$, a manifestation of the Pomeranchuk effect, signals the dominance of low-energy spin superexchange physics. Using exact diagonalization and {\it numerically exact} quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this criterion determines the crossover boundary at $U_{\rm cross}/t=4.0(2)$ for the half-filled two-dimensional Hubbard model. Furthermore, we obtain a consistent boundary independently from the maximum in the antiferromagnetic correlation length, which also arises from the superexchange physics. These two thermal signatures are theoretically unified through the local minimum of thermal entropy versus interaction $U$ at low temperatures. Our results offer a direct, measurable, and physically intuitive framework to identify the Slater-Mott crossover in optical lattice experiments.
item.dc:creator: Mingzhong Lu, Yu-Feng Song, Youjin Deng, Yuan-Yao He

item.title: SmoQyElPhQMC.jl: An open-source Julia package for efficient and scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled models
item.description: arXiv:2606.14425v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce version 1.0 of the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package, an open-source Julia code for performing scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled model Hamiltonians. SmoQyElPhQMC.jl is built upon the SmoQyDQMC.jl codebase and implements improved versions of the algorithms presented in [B. Cohen-Stead \textit{et al}., Phys. Rev. E 105, 065302 (2022)] to enable (near-linear) scalable simulations of a broad class of uncorrelated $e$-ph models both in system size and inverse temperature. By extending the functionality of the flexible scripting interface introduced in SmoQyDQMC.jl, the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package continues to allow users to adapt it to different workflows and interface with other software packages in the Julia ecosystem. The code for this package can be downloaded from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/SmoQySuite/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl or installed using the Julia package manager. The online documentation, including examples, can be obtained from our documentation page at https://smoqysuite.github.io/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl/stable/.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Cohen-Stead, James Neuhaus, Kipton Barros, Thomas A. Maier, Steven Johnston

item.title: High-pressure phase transitions in the quantum spin liquid candidate Na2Co2TeO6 probed by Raman spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2608.25076v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quasi-2D magnet Na2Co2TeO6 (NCTO) is a candidate for a Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquid (KQSL) state. Pressure-tuning in such materials is of interest as a potential method to tune the Kitaev exchange interactions, which are strongly dependent on bond geometry. Here we report a Raman spectroscopic study of NCTO inside a diamond anvil cell (DAC) with pressure applied up to 16.3 GPa. Based on the changes in the Raman modes, this pressure range is divided into three regions. The appearance and disappearance of several modes and changes in the polarization dependence of the representative modes, most prominently above 13.8 GPa, point to pressure-induced phase transitions in this material.
item.dc:creator: Ihsan Ahmed Kolasseri, Maria Mei Ravneb{\ae}k, Subhadip Das, Carl Jonas Linnemann, Haidong Zhou, Christian Frydendahl, Martin Bremholm, Yong P. Chen

item.title: Statistics as a local phase: crystalline order and quench dynamics of emergent dimers in Ising gauge theories
item.description: arXiv:2608.26264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How does the Bose or Fermi statistics of microscopic particles survive when confinement binds them into emergent bosonic composites? We address this question in the strong-coupling limit of a $2+1$D $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory, where charges are confined into tightly bound pairs that can be described by an effective dimer model. We find that the statistics of the underlying matter is encoded entirely in a single local hopping phase $\varphi$ -$0$ for bosons, $\pi$ for fermions. Treating $\varphi$ as a continuous parameter that interpolates between the two, we map the ground-state phase diagram with the help of tensor-network methods. The angle $\varphi$ itself drives a transition between a dimer-superfluid and a dimer-charge density wave state, while the magnetic coupling binds neighboring dimers into resonating pairs, in competition with the inter-dimer repulsion. We identify a novel gapped phase in which dimer pairs crystallize into an ordered pattern of resonating plaquettes. Finally, we propose a quench protocol under which identical dimer configurations evolve in markedly different ways depending on the statistics of their constituents. This provides a dynamical probe of the internal structure of dimers, and allows to detect ordered phases through real-time signatures, within reach of simulators that natively realize bosonic degrees of freedom.
item.dc:creator: Umberto Borla, Riccardo Cioli, Jad C. Halimeh

item.title: A comparison between statistics and 't Hooft anomaly
item.description: arXiv:2609.20813v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Anomalies of generalized symmetries are closely related to the statistics of topological excitations. Truncating a symmetry transformation to a finite region produces an operator that creates symmetry defects on its boundary; we call this a symmetry patch operator. Such operators resemble hopping operators that create topological excitations at the boundary of their support, but this geometric similarity does not justify identifying the two. For finite Abelian groups in one spatial dimension, we prove that if the same family of local operators defines both valid hopping operators and compatible symmetry patches, the type-III component of the anomaly is $-2$ times that of the statistics. We establish a one-to-one correspondence between statistics and anomaly by treating hopping operators as symmetric operators that commute with the global symmetry, following the description of symmetry through the algebra of local symmetric operators. We explain this correspondence through gauging by coupling boundary matter to a Dijkgraaf-Witten gauge field in one higher spatial dimension. Hopping operators act on the gauge-invariant degrees of freedom. After fixing the background gauge field, the residual gauge transformations become the global symmetry, and the gauge invariance of hopping operators becomes the requirement that they commute with this symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Hanyu Xue

item.title: Reformulating Pfaffian Quantum Monte Carlo with the Hybrid Monte Carlo formalism
item.description: arXiv:2609.21631v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pfaffian quantum Monte Carlo extends auxiliary field methods to anomalous fermionic Hamiltonians, opening access to pairing systems and Hubbard--Stratonovich decompositions that are unavailable in determinant formulations. We show that this flexibility can be combined with the global updates of Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC), leading to an algorithm scaling as $\mathcal{O}(N_\tau L^3)$, similar to its determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) counterpart without pseudofermions. The central observation is that the molecular dynamics force depends only on the magnitude of the Pfaffian weight, which admits a determinant representation and leads to a simplified force expression. This construction also yields unequal-time Majorana correlators at essentially no additional cost. We demonstrate the method for the interacting Kitaev chain using the imaginary and symmetric Majorana hopping channel. The resulting noncommuting auxiliary-field bond operators are treated through an even-odd decomposition. Their block structure permits an analytic reduction to a sparse effective interaction matrix of bandwidth two and allows explicit force expressions. Results agree with exact diagonalization and resolve low-energy modes localized at opposite boundaries, together with their increasing overlap near the topological transition of the non-interacting system. These findings establish HMC as an efficient sampling framework for Pfaffian auxiliary-field simulations.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hauschild, Lin Wang, Finn L. Temmen, Thomas Luu

item.title: Direct Charge-4e Superconductivity by Mobilizing Bound Quartets
item.description: arXiv:2609.24445v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A direct charge-\(4e\) superconductor exhibits coherent four-electron order without condensation in any charge-\(2e\) pairing channel. We establish three complementary results. First, a particle-number-conserving Hamiltonian with electron hopping and two-body interactions moves bound quartets efficiently: for electron- and pair-hopping amplitudes \(t\) and \(K\) and local gap \(U_0\), virtual pair transfer produces quartet hopping at order \(K^2/U_0\), whereas electron hopping alone contributes only at order \(t^4/U_0^3\). Second, the microscopic theory identifies an exactly solvable parent Hamiltonian at the phase-separation boundary. Its ground state combines quartet off-diagonal long-range order and finite phase stiffness without pair condensation, while rigorous bounds establish quartet order beyond the parent in a family with explicit quartet transfer. Third, a single convergent strong-coupling expansion simultaneously controls quartet kinetics and thermodynamic stability and rules out condensation in every pair channel of the microscopic model. On bipartite hypercubic lattices at half quartet filling, it yields a parametrically controlled homogeneous phase for \(d\geq2\), with quartet order, a linear collective mode, and gapped charge-\(2e\) excitations. Virtual pair transfer thus enables a direct charge-\(4e\) superconducting ground state without pair condensation.
item.dc:creator: Jin-Tao Jin, Pengfei Li, Yi Zhou

item.title: Re-entrant p-wave superconductivity in a Chern Dartboard Insulator
item.description: arXiv:2609.25205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate an exact theory for a 2-band superconductor with inter-orbital pairing and band Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) interactions. We apply this theory to a Chern dartboard insulator and compute the pair susceptibility and pair correlations analytically. We find that in the insulating phase previously predicted by BCS theory (small pairing strength $g$, chemical potential $\mu$ in the gap), the HK interaction can induce superconductivity, and possibly a Chern dartboard superconductor, by lifting the doubly-occupied band and making it cross the chemical potential. From this HK-induced superconductor, we notice that in a significant parameter range (HK interaction strength $U = 1$, $\mu = 0.5$), an insulator-superconductor-insulator re-entrant transition exists. We isolate the re-entrance to a conflation between HK interactions and inter-orbital pairings.
item.dc:creator: Yueyang Wu, Rebecca Chan, Taylor L. Hughes, Philip W. Phillips

item.title: GEM: An implementation of the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation for simulating interacting quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.32633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present GEM (Ghost Embedding Method), an open-source software package written in Python for computing equilibrium properties of strongly correlated electronic systems within the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation method. GEM provides a computationally efficient framework for studying multi-orbital lattice models. It supports zero- and finite-temperature calculations and symmetry broken phases. It is integrated with the TRIQS ecosystem, providing tools for model construction, self-consistent solution, and evaluation of physical observables. We first detail the method's theoretical formulation, then we present the software architecture, and finally we introduce some practical workflow, which also validates the implementation against established results. In particular, we illustrate the capabilities of GEM through multiorbital and finite-temperature applications and discuss its computational cost relative to more demanding quantum embedding approaches.
item.dc:creator: Samuele Giuli, Tsung-Han Lee, Yong-Xin Yao, Ina Park, Harrison LaBollita, Ivan Pasqua, Nils Wentzell, Nicola Lanat\`a, Olivier Gingras

item.title: Weyl superconductivity from Feshbach resonance in the three-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model
item.description: arXiv:2609.39418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the first experimental realization of the antiferromagnetic phase transition in the three-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model, we present a theoretical study of the model's 3D superconducting phase. By formulating a 3D extension of the Feshbach mechanism, we provide a unified microscopic picture at strong coupling in which pairing is driven by near-resonant bound states of dopants. These long-lived bound states acquire a qualitatively different internal structure in three dimensions compared to their two-dimensional counterparts, giving rise to a distinct superconducting state, namely a time-reversal symmetry breaking $d_{x^2-y^2}+id_{z^2}$ pairing state. We also provide an estimate of the corresponding critical temperature, and provide evidence that the resulting superconducting phase hosts gapless Weyl points. Our results represent a new milestone for the field of quantum simulation, challenging experiments and large-scale numerics alike to test our predictions.
item.dc:creator: Taekyoung Kim, Pit Bermes, Giorgia A. Busin, Fabian Grusdt

item.title: Excitation Spectra of the Frustrated Spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Model via Dual Spin-Sector Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
item.description: arXiv:2610.10454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finding excited states and excitation gaps in frustrated spin systems using Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQE) is complicated by state-ordering inversions. In the frustrated spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model, standard single-sector algorithms like Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD) in $S_z=0$ fail when $J_2/J_1 < 0.25$. In this regime, the lowest-lying excitation in $S_z=0$ is a Triplet ($S=1$), which lies below the Excited Singlet ($S=0$). Standard deflation projects out the ground singlet and converges onto the Triplet state, misidentifying it as the Excited Singlet. Here, this work presents a Dual Spin-Sector VQE framework that resolves these state-ordering inversions applied to frustrated $J_1-J_2$ models on 1D spin chains and 2D rectangular lattices. Firstly, by optimizing the ground Triplet state in the $S_z=1$ sector (where singlet states cannot exist), mapping it into $S_z=0$ via the total spin-lowering operator $S^- = \sum_i S_i^-$, and evaluating a dual-sector penalty cost function, the Excited Singlet ($E_S$) is isolated without variational ambiguity. Numerical state-vector simulations confirm exact convergence to machine precision with unit overlap fidelity. The method captures key physical features, including the gapless phase, the gapless-gapped critical point at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.2411$, the Majumdar-Ghosh dimer point ($J_2/J_1 = 0.50$), and the 2D non-magnetic frustrated regime ($J_2/J_1 \approx 0.40 - 0.60$). Finite-shot sampling simulations and gate-scaling analytics up to $N=100$ qubits demonstrate the resource efficiency and shot resilience of the algorithm for near-term quantum execution.
item.dc:creator: Sk Saniur Rahaman

item.title: Odd-parity surface magnetism in a Kondo insulator
item.description: arXiv:2610.12573v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate a theory of spin-polarized tunneling between a nanowire tip of a topological Kondo insulator SmB$_6$ and the bi-collinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te in which the tunneling conductance which measures magnetic contrast changes sign when the bias is reversed. First we show that no time-reversal-symmetric tip, however strong its spin-momentum locking is, can produce experimentally observed magnetic contrast, which implies that time reversal must be broken at the tip surface. Within a mean-field treatment of the surface theory of SmB$_6$ we find that the interaction between conduction $d$- and $f$-electrons drives a surface phase transition near $T_c\approx10$ K in which the time-reversal-odd component of the Kondo hybridization amplitude condenses in the same symmetry channel as an out-of-plane surface magnetization, gapping out the Dirac surface states. Below the transition the spin-resolved spectral function of each gapped surface Dirac cone is odd in energy about its node. For a charge-neutral apex the Fermi level lies between the surface $\overline{\Gamma}$ and $\overline{X}$ Dirac nodes, so the spin-polarized conductance, which is determined by this function at the bias energy, reverses its sign close to zero bias. This sign change is thus a spectroscopic signature of time-reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of SmB$_6$.
item.dc:creator: Maxim Dzero, Brian M. Andersen

item.title: Converting long-range entanglement into mixture: tensor-network approach to local equilibration
item.description: arXiv:2308.04291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the out-of-equilibrium evolution induced by a quench, fast degrees of freedom generate long-range entanglement that is hard to encode with standard tensor networks. However, local observables only sense such long-range correlations through their contribution to the reduced local state as a mixture. We present a tensor network method that identifies such long-range entanglement and efficiently transforms it into mixture, much easier to represent. In this way, we obtain an effective description of the time-evolved state as a density matrix that captures the long-time behavior of local operators with finite computational resources.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Fr\'ias-P\'erez, Luca Tagliacozzo, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls

item.title: Symmetry defects and gauging for quantum states with matrix product unitary symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2502.20257v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we examine the consequences of the existence of a finite group of matrix product unitary (MPU) symmetries for matrix product states (MPS). We generalize the well-understood picture of onsite unitary symmetries, which give rise to virtual symmetry defects given by insertions of operators in the bonds of the MPS. In the MPU case, we can define analogous defect tensors, this time sitting on lattice sites, that can be created, moved, and fused by local unitary operators. We leverage this formalism to study the gauging of MPU symmetries. We introduce a condition, block independence, under which we can gauge the symmetries by promoting the symmetry defects to gauge degrees of freedom, yielding an MPS of the same bond dimension that supports a local version of the symmetry given by commuting gauge constraints. Whenever block independence does not hold (which happens, in particular, whenever the symmetry representation is anomalous), a modification of our method which we call state-level gauging still gives rise to a locally symmetric MPS by promotion of the symmetry defects, at the expense of producing gauge constraints that do not commute on different sites.
item.dc:creator: Adri\'an Franco-Rubio, Arkadiusz Bochniak, J. Ignacio Cirac

item.title: peaks: a Python package for analysis of angle-resolved photoemission and related spectroscopies
item.description: arXiv:2508.04803v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The electronic band structure, describing the motion and interactions of electrons in materials, dictates the electrical, optical, and thermodynamic properties of solids. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) provides a direct experimental probe of such electronic band structures, and so is widely employed in the study of functional, quantum, and 2D materials. \texttt{peaks} (\textbf{P}ython \textbf{E}lectron spectroscopy \textbf{A}nalysis by \textbf{K}ing group @ \textbf{S}t Andrews) provides a Python package for advanced data analysis of ARPES and related spectroscopic data. It facilitates the fast visualisation and analysis of multi-dimensional datasets, allows for the complex data hierarchy typical to ARPES experiments, and supports lazy data loading and parallel processing, reflecting the ever-increasing data volumes used in ARPES. It is designed to be run in an interactive notebook environment, with extensive inline and pop-out GUI support for data visualisation.
item.dc:creator: Phil D. C. King, Brendan Edwards, Shu Mo, Tommaso Antonelli, Edgar Abarca Morales, Lewis Hart, Liam Trzaska

item.title: Fock-space fragmentation in quenches of disordered interacting fermions
item.description: arXiv:2510.19510v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fock-space fragmentation, as it is currently investigated, primarily originates from specific kinematic constraints or emergent conservation laws in many-body systems with translation invariance. It leads to non-ergodic dynamics and possible breakdown of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Here, we demonstrate that also in disordered systems, such as the XXZ model with random on-site fields, fragmentation appears as a natural concept offering fresh perspectives, for example, on many-body localization (MBL). Specifically, for a given quenched initial state, we identify a potential-energy shell in Fock space, defined by its energy and energy uncertainty, which represents the energetically accessible part of the many-body configuration space. For example, the drastic sample-to-sample fluctuations observed in the weak disorder regime, $W<W_{\mathrm{frag}}$, represent fluctuations of the mass of the shell. Upon increasing disorder, the potential-energy shell becomes increasingly fragmented. Its finite-size evolution exhibits a turnaround flow; extrapolating this flow to the disorder at which the turnaround vanishes provides a heuristic estimate of the strong-fragmentation scale $W_{\mathrm{frag}}$. We conjecture that the fragmentation identified here provides a geometric mechanism contributing to the finite-time slowing down of relaxation observed in studies of disordered interacting systems.
item.dc:creator: Ishita Modak, Rajesh Narayanan, Ferdinand Evers, Soumya Bera

item.title: Anyonic time exchange in hierarchical Hall states: emergent Luttinger scaling and cross-correlations at finite temperature
item.description: arXiv:2510.20592v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We address hierarchical fractional quantum Hall edges coupled by a spatially local quantum point contact within the Unified Nonequilibrium Perturbative (UNEP) framework. Without assuming a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) tunneling correlator, we impose a local anyonic time-exchange (ATE) constraint with phase $\bar{\theta}$, yielding a nonequilibrium fluctuation-dissipation integral equation relating DC tunneling current and noise. For thermal initial states, detailed balance closes this equation for the current. Using the Wiener-Hopf method, we find a unique physical solution of local TLL form, with scaling dimension $\delta$ determined by $\bar{\theta}=\pi\delta\pmod{\pi}$, emerging from the solution rather than being imposed via a TLL correlator. By contrast, ATE and inversion symmetry alone fix the exchange monodromy but not the full transport dynamics. We then study the "anyon collider" beyond Laughlin states at finite temperatures. Detailed balance is broken and noise becomes super-Poissonian, but the relation between nonequilibrium and equilibrium correlators determines current and noise. The output cross-correlation and balanced generalized Fano factor depend on both $\delta$ and statistical phase $\theta$, identical to $\bar{\theta}$ for co-propagating modes with short-range interactions. A temperature-dependent current scale separates the zero-temperature asymptotic regime from the low-current regime, where the balanced Fano factor saturates to a function of $\theta$ and $\delta$ distinct from its zero-temperature value. This latter regime is particularly relevant to ``anyon collider'' experiments. These complementary regimes constrain the statistical phase and scaling dimension, subject to the symmetry $\delta\mapsto1-\delta$ at fixed $\theta$. For independent statistical phase and scaling dimension, the thermal crossover can reverse the sign of output cross-correlations.
item.dc:creator: Aleksander Latyshev, Ines Safi

item.title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe$_2$: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
item.description: arXiv:2512.13877v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One of the recurring hurdles in studying unconventional superconductivity is the challenge of efficiently and conclusively identifying the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in a new material. Uranium ditelluride (UTe$_2$) exhibits an unprecedented number of superconducting phases as a function of pressure and magnetic field, each presumably characterized by a different symmetry of the superconducting gap function. None of these phases has had its symmetry conclusively identified so far. In this article, we report results of an extensive study of the thermal conductivity of UTe$_2$ in its low-field, low-temperature superconducting state as a function of the angle of an applied magnetic field rotated in the $b$-$c$ plane. We observe clear and substantial oscillations in the thermal conductivity as a function of field angle, which naturally suggests the existence of point nodes in the gap. Utilizing the experimentally determined Fermi surface, we are able to model this phenomenon for all the potential gap structures in UTe$_2$ and positively identify the location of these nodes as being along the crystallographic $b$-axis, implying that the superconducting order parameter belongs to the $B_{2u}$ irreducible representation of the crystal point group. The clarity of this result will accelerate the identification of other superconducting phases in UTe$_2$, and guide future studies through the use of high resolution field-angle-dependent measurements.
item.dc:creator: Ian M. Hayes, Elliot Fang, Shanta R. Saha, Vivek Mishra, P. J. Hirschfeld, Johnpierre Paglione

item.title: Symmetric Mass Generation as a Multicritical Point with Enhanced Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2512.24836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explore the phase diagram of a lattice fermion model that exhibits three distinct phases: a massless fermion phase, a massive fermion phase with spontaneous symmetry breaking induced by a fermion bilinear condensate, and a massive fermion phase with symmetric mass generation. Using the fermion-bag Monte Carlo method on large cubical lattices, we find evidence for traditional second-order critical points separating the first two and the latter two phases. Remarkably, these critical points appear to merge at a multicritical point with enhanced symmetry when the symmetry breaking parameter is tuned to zero, giving rise to the recently discovered direct second-order transition between the massless and symmetric massive fermion phases.
item.dc:creator: Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Marina K. Marinkovic

item.title: Geometry-Induced Skin Effect in Electron Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.17229v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In ultra-clean 2d materials electron viscosity is as important as Ohmic dissipation and electron transport exhibits hydrodynamic features. Using a simple framework of Brinkman equations we find that hydrodynamic electron flows give rise to a geometric skin effect: sharp obstacles locally enhance the current suppressing it far from the edges where the flow is unobstructed. This effect arises within hydrodynamic transport with finite momentum relaxation and does not rely on ballistic dynamics. Our results provide a natural hydrodynamic interpretation of edge-enhanced and double-bump current profiles observed in constricted geometries. By comparing with recent scanning NV magnetometry experiments on gated graphene, we demonstrate that such flow patterns are consistent with viscous hydrodynamics shaped by geometry, clarifying the role of geometric effects in the interpretation of electronic flow experiments.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Paw{\l}owski, Piotr Sur\'owka, Konstantin Zarembo

item.title: Symmetric Gapped States and Symmetry-Enforced Gaplessness in 3-dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2602.12335v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a comprehensive framework for characterizing the infrared (IR) phases of a fermionic quantum theory in three spatial dimensions, based on its quantum anomalies associated with a finite symmetry. We uncover a fundamental dichotomy among these anomalies: the first class of anomalies can always be realized by symmetric gapped states, while the second class can never be realized by gapped states without breaking the given symmetry, establishing the phenomenon of symmetry-enforced gaplessness in these settings. Moreover, using the construction of symmetry extension, we construct the candidate gapped states that theories with the first class of anomalies can flow to in the IR. As an application, we provide concrete predictions of the candidate IR phases of (3+1)-dimensional gauge theories based on our results. Our results also suggest that systems with discrete chiral anomalies cannot be gapped out by adding arbitrary bosonic degrees of freedom.
item.dc:creator: Arun Debray, Matthew Yu, Weicheng Ye

item.title: Phase diagram of a lattice fermion model with symmetric mass generation
item.description: arXiv:2602.18360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the phase structure of a model containing two flavors of massless staggered fermions interacting through two independent four-fermion couplings, UI and UB, formulated on a three-dimensional Euclidean space-time lattice. At UB = 0, this model is known to exhibit a direct second-order quantum phase transition between a massless fermion (MF) phase and a phase in which fermions acquire masses through the mechanism commonly referred to as symmetric mass generation (SMG). We demonstrate that introducing a small nonzero value of UB qualitatively alters this structure: the single exotic transition at UB = 0 splits into two distinct, conventional transitions, separated by an intermediate phase in which fermion masses arise through the standard mechanism of spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB). The first of these is a Gross-Neveu transition separating the MF phase from the SSB-induced massive phase, while the second is a three-dimensional XY transition between the SSB phase and the SMG phase. Using the fermion-bag Monte Carlo method, we verify that the critical exponents associated with both transitions are consistent with the literature, thereby yielding a quantitative characterization of the resulting phase structure of the model.
item.dc:creator: Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Marina K. Marinkovic

item.title: Entanglement in the $\theta$-vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2603.29287v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $\theta$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $\theta=\pi$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $\theta=\pi$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $\theta=\pi$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix. We observe agreement in the infrared sector, indicating that the entanglement Hamiltonian is well approximated by a spatially weighted Hamiltonian. Finally, we discuss possible applications to entanglement in topological insulators and quantum wires. In this work, we used the chirally rotated formulation of the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. We identify an additive vacuum-energy artifact induced by the discretization of the chirally rotated lattice and derive its exact free-lattice form to subtract it in the continuum limit.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Grieninger, Dmitri E. Kharzeev, Eliana Marroquin

item.title: Pressure-induced decoupling of the pseudogap and superconductivity in a bilayer cuprate
item.description: arXiv:2604.10207v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The physical origin of the pseudogap in cuprate superconductors, whether a precursor to superconductivity or a distinct intertwined order, remains an open question. Although hydrostatic pressure provides a clean tuning parameter, probing the relevant energy scales under compression has remained experimentally elusive. Here, we employ ultrafast optical spectroscopy to track the non-equilibrium quasiparticle dynamics of slightly underdoped Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+{\delta}}$ up to 37 GPa. By disentangling the pseudogap and superconducting relaxation channels in the time domain, we uncover a contrasting pressure evolution: despite an increase in carrier density, the pseudogap thermal onset (T$^*$) rises monotonically, whereas its energy gap ($\Delta_{PG}$) is continuously suppressed. Conversely, the critical temperature (T$_C$) and the superconducting gap ($\Delta_{SC}$) exhibit a synchronized dome-like trajectory. The effective coupling ratio 2$\Delta_{SC}$/k$_B$T$_C$ collapses abruptly from ~10 toward the weak-coupling d-wave limit, signifying a crossover from a phase-fluctuating two-dimensional regime to a globally coherent three-dimensional state. Upon compression to 37 GPa, the superconducting condensate is completely quenched into an insulating-like state, yet the pseudogap persists. The extended phase diagram reveals an unambiguous decoupling between the pseudogap and superconductivity, imposing stringent constraints on microscopic theories of high-temperature superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Yanghao Meng, Wenjin Mao, Liucheng Chen, Elbert E. M. Chia, Yifeng Yang, Tao Xiang, Jianlin Luo, Lin Zhao, Xingjiang Zhou, Xiaohui Yu, Xinbo Wang

item.title: Entanglement dynamics after quenches with inhomogeneous Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2605.01595v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate entanglement dynamics in bipartite systems governed by inhomogeneous Hamiltonians of the form $H = H_L + H_R$, where $H_{L/R}$ acts only on the left or right region and is homogeneous within each region. Focusing on the XX chain and the transverse-field Ising chain, we derive analytical formulas for the entanglement entropy between the two regions in the hydrodynamic limit of long times. In this regime, fermions incident on the interface undergo scattering, generating entanglement between reflected and transmitted modes. The resulting quasiparticle picture is controlled by the transmission coefficient, which we obtain analytically by solving the stationary lattice Schr\"odinger equation. Due to the bounded dispersion, strong inhomogeneity suppresses both transport and entanglement growth. We benchmark our analytical predictions against numerical simulations in paradigmatic setups. Finally, we extend the analysis to the interacting XXZ chain using tDMRG. The numerical data show qualitative agreement with the quadratic case: entanglement growth remains suppressed in the strongly inhomogeneous limit. Notably, however, entanglement continues to increase even when transport is suppressed, at least at intermediate times.

item.title: Multifractality at the Integer Quantum Hall Transition: Acquittal of the Parabolic Law
item.description: arXiv:2606.21679v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stationary wave functions at the integer quantum Hall transition are known to be multifractal, but the exact form of the multifractality spectrum has remained a subject of debate. While conformal field theory arguments predict a parabolic law, numerical simulations show deviations from parabolicity. We resolve this discrepancy by pointing out that powers of the local wave intensity fail to obey the Gaussian Free Field and Abelian Fusion Hypothesis assumed in earlier analysis. Rather, due to the non-Abelian nature of the underlying effective field theory, wave intensity correlators are dressed by insertions of background charge distributed uniformly in space. An exact expression for the $q$-moments of point-contact generated eigenstates is presented. Numerical tests are performed for the critical Chalker-Coddington network model on a rectangular torus. Our results are in precise agreement with the predictions of conformal symmetry realized as a level-4 current algebra.
item.dc:creator: Sen Mu, Abbas Ali Saberi, Martin R. Zirnbauer

item.title: Spin-fluctuation-mediated unconventional $d_{xy}$-wave superconductivity in ThFeAsN from first-principles
item.description: arXiv:2607.14677v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Superconducting (SC) pairing mechanism, origin of high $T_c$ and symmetry of SC order parameter in Fe-based superconductors are among the important unsolved problems in condensed matter and materials physics. We study the SC properties of ThFeAsN, a Fe-based high $T_c$ superconductor, by {\it ab initio} superconducting density functional theory calculations with electron-phonon coupling, screened static and dynamic electron-electron Coulomb repulsion and spin fluctuation (SF) mediated pair-interaction fully taken into account. Our calculations reveal that ThFeAsN is a SF-mediated multiband superconductor with the calculated $T_c$ of 22.4 K and the $d_{xy}$-wave SC order parameter with different signs on different Fermi surface sheets, in consistent with experiments. We also present distinct SC properties such as quasiparticle density of states and ultrasonic attenuation coefficient which can be immediately verified by experiments.
item.dc:creator: Guang-Yu Guo, Jau-Wen Liu, Mitsuaki Kawamura

item.title: Multicomponent Magnetic Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2608.26104v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spatial textures of magnetic order, such as domain walls and skyrmions, are fundamental objects in magnetism. In rhombohedral multilayer graphene, magnetic order involves spin and valley degrees of freedom, opening the possibility of qualitatively new spatial textures. Here, we explore this possibility through a microscopic study of a one-dimensional domain wall in the valley-imbalanced quarter-metal phase of rhombohedral graphene. We uncover two different classes of domain walls. One resembles a conventional magnetic domain wall, locally rotating between the two bulk states, whereas the other is intrinsically multicomponent and explores states that are not occupied in either bulk domain. Which texture is realized is controlled by the competition between intervalley Hund's coupling and spin-orbit coupling, and we identify experimental signatures to distinguish them. For a superconducting junction formed across the wall, we further show that the superconducting phase difference couples directly to the intervalley-coherent phase of the texture, allowing precession of this internal phase to generate a voltage. This mechanism provides an explanation for the resistive domain walls recently observed in chiral superconductors [arXiv2605.13303] and predicts accompanying magnetization oscillations that could be detected using GHz-frequency AC probes. Our theory establish a microscopic connection between multicomponent magnetic textures, their internal dynamics, and superconducting transport.
item.dc:creator: Mainak Das, Nemin Wei, Chunli Huang

item.title: Integrable Chiral Quantum Field Theories with Spacetime-Dependent Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2609.13377v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a class of integrable chiral fermionic quantum field theories with interactions that depend on both space and time. The construction starts from a unitary, regular, difference-form two-body scattering matrix satisfying braiding unitarity and the Yang--Baxter equation. Each freely moving right- or left-moving particle carries a characteristic coordinate that remains constant along its trajectory, and the scattering matrix depends on differences of these coordinates. The many-body amplitudes form a discrete connection over the coordinate-ordering sectors. The Yang--Baxter equation gives local path independence, while periodic winding on a spatial circle produces quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (qKZ) difference equations expressing global flatness. Once a reference amplitude satisfying the exchange and qKZ constraints is specified, these transport equations determine the exact wavefunction in every fixed-particle-number sector. Independent reparametrizations of the right- and left-moving characteristics give couplings that depend on both space and time. For the chiral $SU(2)$ Gross--Neveu realization, we solve the qKZ equations for this full characteristic family using off-shell Bethe vectors. The resulting amplitudes are written in the characteristic labels, and their pullbacks give exact many-body wavefunctions for the corresponding space-time-dependent couplings. The two-body amplitude is a ratio of Gamma functions that resums the phase shifts from successive scattering processes. Equal-slope affine maps give a spatially homogeneous specialization in which the coupling depends only on time, and the Bethe ansatz with constant coupling is recovered when the qKZ step vanishes.

item.title: Locally optimized variational evolution for quantum many-body systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.20802v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum many-body dynamics is difficult to simulate because the global wavefunction develops extensive complexity, whereas local observables may retain only an intrinsic, system-size-independent complexity. This distinction is especially relevant in thermalizing systems, where local subsystems lose microscopic information and relax towards equilibrium. We introduce a variational time-evolution principle that exploits this separation by replacing global-state fidelity with a cost function defined on local reduced density matrices. The resulting locally optimized matrix-product-state (LOMPS) algorithm retains coherent short-time dynamics while using the simplification generated by thermalization at later times, and admits closed-form equations of motion analogous to the time-dependent variational principle. The same principle yields a quantum-classical algorithm in which a quantum processor evaluates the local cost and a noise-robust classical procedure performs the optimization. Proof-of-principle implementations on Quantinuum H2 and IBM Heron processors recover the characteristic local dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Carolin Wille, Maximilian Marvell, Lauren Stewart, Maximillian Murphy, Vinul Wimalaweera, Lesley Gover, Andrew G. Green

item.title: The equivalence of topological indices for $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric quantum spin chains
item.description: arXiv:2609.34119v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases in quantum spin chains are distinguished by topological indices. Ogata's operator-algebraic indices apply to a broad range of symmetry classes without requiring continuous symmetry, whereas the elementary twist index of Tasaki requires $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. We prove their equivalence in the common setting of integer-spin chains with on-site $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry and a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, without assuming translation invariance or a matrix product representation. A charge-fluctuation estimate yields a strong-limit construction of half-chain rotations with their phases fixed. An exact group commutator identity then identifies the Ogata index with the limit of local twist expectations and gives an explicit error bound. This provides a computable formula for the index when a lower bound on the gap and the relevant ground-state expectations are available. Combining the equivalence with a recent boundary-field gap theorem of OpenAI and our earlier twist-index calculation, we obtain a spin-rotation-invariant locally-unique gapped ground state of the infinite $S=1$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain with both indices equal to $-1$, without assuming infinite-volume uniqueness. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy, while ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the development of the proof.
item.dc:creator: Hal Tasaki

item.title: Quasiparticle-resolved variational theory of Andreev spin qubits
item.description: arXiv:2610.08557v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An Andreev spin qubit stores a single unpaired spin, yet its coupling to the superconducting phase can be dominated by coherent virtual quasiparticle pairs. We develop a continuum variational description of the odd-parity doublet in a quantum-dot Josephson junction with Coulomb interaction and spin-dependent background tunneling. Retaining configurations with up to two Bogoliubov quasiparticles provides compact analytical expressions for energies and wavefunctions. We benchmark the results against numerical renormalization group calculations and identify sources of error. We obtain closed-form expressions for the conventional and spin-dependent Josephson couplings. Despite their small probability, two-quasiparticle configurations, through coherence with the zero-quasiparticle component, supply exactly half of the leading spin-dependent Josephson coupling even without Coulomb repulsion and dominate it as the repulsion grows. Spin-orbit-induced spin transfer between the dot and the leads produces a Josephson-current contribution that is common to both qubit states and finite at zero phase bias when the dot and lead Zeeman energies differ. We also map the localization of the virtual quasiparticles and the spin density in the leads. The results connect strongly correlated quantum-dot models to effective Hamiltonians used for Andreev-spin-qubit circuits and clarify how the wavefunction structure determines their couplings.
item.dc:creator: Teodor Ili\v{c}in, Rok \v{Z}itko

item.title: Correspondence between Asymptotic Quantum Many-Body Scars in Closed Systems and Diffusive Nambu-Goldstone Modes in Open Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.09662v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hydrodynamic relaxation in open quantum many-body systems can be understood in terms of diffusive Nambu--Goldstone (NG) modes associated with strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SWSSB). Here, we find a common structure underlying weak ergodicity breaking in closed quantum systems and diffusive hydrodynamics in open quantum systems. We establish a spectral correspondence between the parent Hamiltonian of rainbow quantum many-body scar (RQMBS) states in closed systems and the effective Lindbladian of strongly dissipative open systems with strong $U(1)$ symmetry and local charge-dephasing Lindblad operators. For broad classes of spin, fermionic, and bosonic systems, we construct asymptotic RQMBS (ARQMBS) states. Within the enlarged scar subspace, the parent Hamiltonian admits a local Rokhsar--Kivelson-type frustration-free decomposition. A single-mode variational construction gives an $O(k^2)$ upper bound on its lowest excitation energy and yields states satisfying the defining ARQMBS criteria: orthogonality, vanishing energy variance, and characteristic entanglement scaling. Under vectorization, RQMBS states are mapped to maximally mixed infinite-temperature states in fixed-charge sectors, which exhibit long-range SWSSB order under finite-density conditions. Assuming uniformly bounded positive transition rates, the effective Lindbladian has the same local projectors as the parent Hamiltonian but with positive transition-dependent weights, yielding two-sided spectral bounds and the same system-size scaling of their gaps. For uniform rates, the two operators are proportional to each other and their eigenmodes coincide. Therefore, an exact quadratic parent-Hamiltonian branch maps directly to a diffusive NG mode. Our results connect different mechanisms of slow relaxation in closed and open quantum many-body systems.
